parts.description: A single shallot with a teardrop shape, covered in dry, papery, reddish-brown outer skin. It features small, dry root remnants at the base and a twisted, tapering top.
parts.reasoning: The object is a shallot, a small, teardrop-shaped bulb vegetable. Shallots are relatively lightweight and have a density similar to water, perhaps slightly less due to their organic structure and layers, estimated around 900 kg/m^3. A typical shallot weighs approximately 20-30 grams (0.025 kg). The surface is a dry, papery skin, which would have a moderate static and dynamic friction coefficient when interacting with other surfaces, lower than rubber but higher than smooth plastic (estimated static: 0.45, dynamic: 0.35). Restitution (bounciness) would be quite low as it's a solid, slightly compressible organic mass, estimated at 0.1. For simulation in Isaac Sim, a convex hull is a highly appropriate and performant collider type for this shape, as the overall geometry is generally convex, ignoring the minor intricacies of the roots and the very tip. Standard contact and rest offsets are suitable. Since it's a single rigid body, articulated properties are not applicable.
